text.p: Wants his docks quiet and his friends paid. Offers a berth, a rumour, or an introduction on any station where the longshore trust him, which is most of them. Berthmaster. If the crew starts a firefight on his deck, the offer ends.

id-00001.desc: She treats the crew for the cost of the supplies, and one favour later. A Down character in her care wakes with 1d6 Stamina. She does not do this twice in a row for nothing.

id-00002.desc: For a fee or a favour he names who is buying a given kind of salvage this month, and what they will not ask.

text.p: Wants to die on a rock he chose, not in a yard he owes. Offers parts, a quiet buyer, and the truth about a wreck if he has been there. A belter fixer. His price is credits, or a tool he does not have.

Wants the Accord's salvage law applied in the open. Offers a lawful rescue reward paid in full, and her testimony if a rival tries to bury a living passenger. She is an enemy only to a crew that files a derelict with someone still breathing on it. Inspector out of Port Sable.

A job the crew can finish in a session has five parts. Write them down before you play. The players do not need to see the page.

list.li: 1. The patron. Someone with a name, a want, and a reason to hire this crew. A contact in this book will do.
2. The rival. Someone who wants the same thing, already moving. They arrive when the clock says, not when the fight would be fair.
3. The clock. Three tasks to get there (Astrogation, Pilot, and one more). Each failure costs time. Say the time out loud.
4. The find. What is actually there. It should change the job: a living person turns salvage into a rescue; a thread spool turns a tow into a decision.
5. The payoff. Credits, a favour, a Mark, and a thread for next time. Experience is 2 each for the job, plus 1 for a hard thing done right.

text.p: Offer the deal before the shooting. Most rivals in the Reach would rather be paid.
When the crew cracks a hold and you have not already decided what is in it, roll 2d6 once for the hold, then invent the crate that matches.

tr.td: Thread-eaten scrap. 200 credits if anyone will buy it. A nest of thread lice if anyone powers the ring.
Personal effects. A story, a name, and maybe 100 credits.
A ship's locker: tape, foam, a breather, a lamp. Useful, not rich.
Rations and a medkit. Someone meant to come back.
Ordinary trade goods, 1d6 x 1,000 credits at a fair port.
Yard parts, 2d6 x 1,000 credits to a yard, half that to anyone else.
A data slate with a route. Sell it for 3,000, or keep a Boon on one Astrogation in that sector.
A locked strongbox. Electronics or Mechanics (Hard). Then roll again, and use the higher idea.
Someone alive. The job is a rescue. The Accord pays about a tenth of what the cargo would have.
A sealed case the Combine will bid on: 2d6 x 5,000 credits. Someone follows the seller.
A beacon that should be dark. Another crew is already counting the days.

text.p: A thread spool is the expensive case. It is a black-market skein part, legal to own, not legal to spin without a yard stamp (a fine, not a hanging). Mounted by an Engineering task (Hard, one hour), the ship's next jump takes three days instead of seven. On a failure the drive is ruined until a yard rebuilds it. The Combine pays about 30,000 credits and remembers the name. A bare spool carried next to a powered skein ring makes every task in that compartment Desperate until one of them is moved or powered down.
A claim beacon left on a hull shouts a filing. If it was planted earlier than the crew's stamp, the argument at the registry gets worse. Electronics (Hard) silences one.
Prices are a guide. A hungry port pays less. A yard that needs the part pays more.
Each of these is a session if you play the clock and the choice. Use the salvage roll if a hold is still a mystery.

The ice run. Lale Yee pays 1,500 credits to get a cold-crate of blood and antibiotics to a belt clinic before a fever does. A pirate skiff wants the crate because the clinic's buyer is late on protection. The find: the patient is a Combine clerk's child, and Hess Kade is already on the way to collect the family, not the medicine.

The buoy. The Accord pays 2,000 to restart a navigation buoy that has gone quiet. Rook Tal is stripping it. The find: a vac-suit clipped to the buoy's far side, still broadcasting a claim chip. The person inside has been dead nine days. The chip is a filing on a hull nobody has found.

Yard night. Harun Vey wants photographs of a coolant swap at the Combine yard, not a theft. The yard boss is the rival, and the watch is awake. The find: the cheap cores are real, and the Kestrel's Due was not the only ship sold them.

Two stamps. Ivo Quill shows the crew two filings on one hull, an hour apart. He will delay the second if they go and see whether anyone is alive. This is A Lamp in the Rock, if you want it played out.

Missed the boat. A passenger pays 1,000 to be put aboard a liner that has already spun up its ring. The rival is the liner's purser, who was paid to leave them. The find: the passenger's papers are good, and the purser's second payment came from Hess Kade.

The marker. Old Cade asks the crew to carry a debt marker to a rock and pay it off with parts he has boxed. Hess Kade meets them there and says the marker is forged, which is half true. The find: the box is real yard parts, and the forgery is Cade's only lie. Paying the true debt costs the parts. Keeping them makes an enemy of both.
